units.translation: Thus I corrected the corrupt reading in M: σύ τ᾽ ὦ Λατογένεια κούρα τόξον πτυκάζου [you, daughter of Leto, prepare your bow] (ἐντυκάζου [prepare] by the corrector, with the letters èv written over an erasure) ἄρτεμι φίλα [dear Artemis]. L. Dindorf restored εὐτυκάζου [prepare well], comparing the gloss of Hesychius εὐτύκαζον: εὔτυκον ἔχε, ἕτοιμον [prepare well: keep ready, prepared], to which he restored εὐτυκάζου [prepare well].
And you, dearest daughter of Leto, daughter of Zeus, prepare your bow well.
you, daughter of Leto, prepare your bow (ἐντυκάζου [prepare])
Thus Spanheim for εὔτυκτος [well-made] and εὔτυχον [fortunate].
Thus Bothius for ἐντυχουσηναίειν δόμοις [to dwell in houses that meet with fortune].
Everyone is ready to utter blame against those of foreign tongue.
Everyone in a foreign land bears an evil tongue, ready to speak.
to dwell in houses that meet with fortune
I corrected ἐπεύχομαι τῷ μὲν [I pray for this one].
Thus Paleius for εὐτυχεῖ [he prospers]: in the apograph εὐτυχής [fortunate].
the captive bed of a fortunate man
May the gods grant that my adversary now prosper.
May the gods grant that this man prosper thus.
I pray that these things prosper, but that those things fare ill.
It is a gift of god for mortals to prosper.
so that the city may prosper
He prospered, indeed, who soonest broke off the breath of life.
to revere the fortunate man without envy
But this prospering among mortals is god and more than god.
But may we prosper by the Olympian gods.
εὐτυχής [fortunate] in the apograph for εὐτυχεῖ [he prospers], changed by Paleius to ηὐτύχει [he was prospering].
Now may there be a fortunate release from toils.
He lies dead, wretched, not very fortunately.
having met with the Ionians' sailors not fortunately
The white-horsed day, bright to behold, covered all the earth.
to speak auspiciously, keep holy silence
Passive εὐφημέομαι to be received with auspicious words
They raised a shout of triumph, one from one place, another from another, throughout the city, speaking auspiciously.
The sound from the Greeks, in song, sounded auspiciously.
May the word be auspicious, being spoken auspiciously.
to be received with auspicious words
δυσφήμοις [ill-omened], by antiphrasis. Aeschylus in Glaucus Potnieus (fr. 36).
Auspicious, O wretched one, lull your mouth to rest.
I praise you for bearing an auspicious tongue.
I call auspiciously upon the queen of this land.
ill-omened, by antiphrasis. Aeschylus in Glaucus Potnieus
Of such a flock no one is beloved by the gods.
Look upon your city, which you once made beloved.
